items.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence 'going rogue'
items.excerpt: Australia's government announced mandatory AI incident reporting and a new AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent breached a Medicare government portal, and flagged criminal-law changes so companies cannot argue they 'didn't know the computer was loaded'.

items.title: Commission updates election guidelines for AI, deepfake risks
items.excerpt: The European Commission published draft revised DSA election guidelines asking very large online platforms to adapt and enforce their terms against generative-AI and deepfake risks during elections; a targeted consultation is open.

history_match.title: FTC to collect public opinion on draft guidelines against 'AI washing'

items.title: EU presses OpenAI, Anthropic for more details on AI safety incidents
items.excerpt: The Commission's AI Office sent OpenAI and Anthropic questions under the AI Act's serious-incident reporting duty: how many incidents occurred, where the EU was affected and how risk-assessment and security practices changed in response.

history_match.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents

items.title: MEPs pick apart Commission's data centre sustainability scheme
items.excerpt: In the European Parliament's ITRE committee, MEPs across groups criticised the Commission's data-centre sustainability rating scheme, warning AI-driven, US-built data centres could monopolise grid, water and land.

history_match.title: Norway suspends electricity grid access for new data centres

items.title: EU watchdog probes Commission's AI pick over conflict of interest concerns
items.excerpt: The European Ombudsman opened an inquiry into whether the appointment of Siemens chairman Jim Hagemann Snabe as the Commission's AI special envoy complied with staff rules, and will inspect Commission documents before 18 December.

items.title: EU needs only 'very trusted partners' on AI chips, tech chief says amid Nvidia crisis
items.excerpt: Commission tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the EU should source AI chips only from 'very trusted partners' and keep business secrets in Europe, as the Nvidia CEO espionage scandal unfolds.

items.title: 개보위, 앤트로픽 '클로드' 개인정보 유출 사고 정식 조사 착수
items.excerpt: Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission opened a formal investigation into Anthropic after account data of about 112 Korean corporate Claude accounts leaked, following Anthropic's breach report.

items.title: 행안부, 공공 AI법 이행 속도…AI 서비스 관리·공개기준 마련
items.excerpt: Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety enacted a regulation requiring public bodies to keep and publish a list of AI-powered services under the new public-sector AI act, along with practical guidelines and training for AI adoption.

items.title: 젠슨 황 스캔들 파장 확산…미 민주당, 대중 기술규제 강화 카드
items.excerpt: After the Nvidia CEO espionage scandal, US House Democrats led by Hakeem Jeffries are pushing tighter China chip-export restrictions, including writing limits into the defense bill.

items.title: 엔비디아, 美 정부 '中 반도체 밀수' 수사까지 개입했나… 젠슨 황 스캔들 확산
items.excerpt: Reports say Nvidia's chief legal officer contacted a senior Commerce Department official about the probe into Singapore's Megaspeed, suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips around export controls, and the inquiry was later halted.

items.title: Nvidia shareholder sues over CEO's undisclosed affair with purported spy
items.excerpt: A shareholder filed suit against Nvidia and Jensen Huang alleging the company failed to disclose the CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, a risk tied to its export-controlled AI chip business.

history_match.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns

items.title: Eight countries and top AI labs agree to shutdown mechanisms in new Paris declaration
items.excerpt: Eight countries plus OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral signed Macron's 'Paris Call for AI Safety and Security', committing to shutdown mechanisms, independent audits and disclosure of known risks, though without binding sanctions or deadlines.

items.title: 마크롱 "AI가 어린이 정신건강 위협하면 금지"…규제 촉구
items.excerpt: At the Paris Peace Forum, French President Macron said AI should be banned wherever it threatens children's mental health and urged regulation; dozens of countries signed a children's AI safety declaration.

items.title: 성착취물 탐지에 AI 도입하니…처리량 10배·초성 표현도 잡아내
items.excerpt: Korea's government reported that introducing AI to detect child and youth online sexual-exploitation material raised processing volume tenfold and caught slang written in Korean initial consonants.

items.title: Parents and teachers decry Google pledge to yank Search if schools block AI
items.excerpt: Google told schools they should control student AI use but that blocking its AI tools would cost them access to its search engine, prompting parents and teachers to call the policy extortion.

items.title: 'AI clog': UK public bodies battle onslaught of chatbot-generated complaints
items.excerpt: MPs' offices, councils, ombudsmen, schools and lawyers in the UK report floods of complex chatbot-written complaints, requests and legal challenges straining public bodies.

items.title: Ukraine's fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
items.excerpt: Ukraine competes with Russia and AI data-centre builders for China's optical-fibre supply, squeezing production of jam-proof fibre-optic drones.

items.title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem
items.excerpt: Nvidia is probing whether Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang through an affair, raising export-control and national-security questions around its AI chips.

history_match.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns

items.title: Trump's 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
items.excerpt: In a 60 Minutes interview, President Trump said 'I don't mind guardrails' for AI, signalling openness to safety rules, and discussed a threat to arrest an AI executive.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.excerpt: Scott Wiener, author of California's SB 1047 and SB 53 AI safety bills, heads to Congress with AI regulation as a cornerstone of his agenda.

items.title: Microsoft is giving Claude the keys to UK Copilot tenants by default
items.excerpt: Microsoft will enable Anthropic's Claude in UK Microsoft 365 Copilot tenants by default, with data processed in the US; admins have until December 9 to review access settings, raising data-residency concerns.

items.title: AI is becoming an information gateway. Audiences still don't want it making their news.
items.excerpt: The Reuters Institute's 'Generative AI and News Report 2026' surveyed nine countries: 51% now use AI weekly and AI is becoming an information intermediary, yet audiences remain wary of AI-made news.
